Subject: Re: Pricing structure clarification for VPC/on-prem

Amelia — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below and I attached a draft quote that separates line items. Full SOW to follow once we lock the SKU mix.

- Migration/installation: one-time professional services line (SOW) — typically expensed. We usually price as a scoped fixed-fee (hours + travel if on-prem).
- Platform fee: recurring subscription for the Private control plane and orchestration; we can structure as a capitalizable fee for accounting, yes.
- Support tiers (summary):
  * Standard: business-hours ticketing, 24h severity-1 response target, monthly patch windows.
  * Premium: 24/7 monitoring + 2h severity-1 response SLA, prioritized escalation, quarterly runbooks.
  * Enterprise (Platinum): named TAM, on-call rotation + 1h severity-1 response, extended change window support and quarterly onsite reviews.

Discounting: we can offer staged discounts tied to committed GPU-hours (12/24/36 month bands) or an annual committed spend. Example in the attached quote shows 12% off list for a 24-month commit at our mid-tier GPU profile.

I[0m'll loop in Marcus for quantization/kernel licensing notes (he[0m led the private runtime pricing).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing structure clarification for VPC/on-prem

Soojin / team — quick clarification on two technical-commercial items requested by Nebula:

1) Quantization / optimized kernel add-on: For some customers we price an optional license for enterprise-only optimized kernels (low-level vendor kernels we maintain) as a line item — it's typically called the "optimization pack". It is optional and can be included in the platform fee or shown separately.

2) Metering: If Nebula wants nightly metered usage reporting to reconcile GPU-hours vs committed hours, we can include a usage export and monthly reconciliation clause in the contract (adds minimal ops overhead, but avoids disputes).

Recommendation: Show the optimization pack as an optional annual SKU so procurement can decide. If they plan to use it broadly, we can bake a 20% bundle discount when included with a three-year commit.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product Pricing, Redwood Inference

Hello — addressing procurement items: 

- Invoicing: yes, we can issue a milestone invoice for migration on acceptance sign-off and then quarterly invoices for the platform fee in arrears. We'll include invoice terms in the Master Services Agreement.
- Price protection: we can guarantee a max list-price increase of 5% YoY for a 36-month committed contract. That will be binding in the commercial terms.
- SOW deliverables: we'll add an 'Acceptance & Performance Criteria' section with an install checklist, a P99 latency test (baseline and post-install), and a 15-business-day window for remediation if acceptance criteria are not met.

I'll attach a sample MSA and a redline-friendly SOW template for your legal team. If procurement would like, we can offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of the migration fee if we miss SLA on initial production rollout (remediation & credit capped).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) On the optimization pack: would you consider including it at no charge for the first 12 months if we go with a 36-month commit at the proposed tiers? That removes a blocker for our engineering team.

If you can confirm those two items and send the redlineable MSA/SOW, we can route to legal tomorrow.

Amelia
